heading.en: Where did the first living thing come from?

hook.en: Look at the night sky and you look back billions of years. Somewhere in that long history, simple chemicals on the young Earth became the first life.
hook.kn: ರಾತ್ರಿಯ ಆಕಾಶವನ್ನು ನೋಡಿದಾಗ ನಾವು ಕೋಟ್ಯಂತರ ವರ್ಷಗಳ ಹಿಂದಕ್ಕೆ ನೋಡುತ್ತೇವೆ. ಆ ದೀರ್ಘ ಇತಿಹಾಸದಲ್ಲಿ ಸರಳ ರಾಸಾಯನಿಕಗಳು ಮೊದಲ ಜೀವವಾದವು.

title.en: The early Earth and theories of origin

body.en: The universe is about 20 billion years old and the Earth about 4.5 billion years. Early Earth had no proper atmosphere; water vapour, methane, carbon dioxide and ammonia were released from molten matter. Life appeared about 500 million years after the Earth formed, almost four billion years back. Panspermia proposed that spores came from outer space. Spontaneous generation, the idea that life came from decaying matter, was disproved by Louis Pasteur: killed yeast in pre-sterilised flasks gave no new life, while flasks open to air did.
body.kn: ವಿಶ್ವ ಸುಮಾರು 2000 ಕೋಟಿ ವರ್ಷ, ಭೂಮಿ ಸುಮಾರು 450 ಕೋಟಿ ವರ್ಷ ಹಳೆಯದು. ಸುಮಾರು 400 ಕೋಟಿ ವರ್ಷಗಳ ಹಿಂದೆ ಜೀವ ಕಾಣಿಸಿಕೊಂಡಿತು. ಲೂಯಿ ಪಾಶ್ಚರ್ ಸ್ವಯಂಜನನ ಸಿದ್ಧಾಂತವನ್ನು ತಳ್ಳಿಹಾಕಿದರು.

say.en: A timeline, not to scale: the universe about 20 billion years old, the Earth 4.5 billion, life about 4 billion years ago, cells about 2 billion years ago.
Three ideas: spores from space, panspermia; life from decaying matter, spontaneous generation, which Pasteur disproved; and chemical evolution, from Oparin and Haldane.
Miller sealed methane, hydrogen, ammonia and water vapour in a flask at 800 degrees Celsius and passed electric sparks through it.
After a week, amino acids had formed in the flask: organic molecules can arise from simple ones, as Oparin and Haldane proposed.

title.en: Chemical evolution: Oparin, Haldane and Miller

body.en: Oparin of Russia and Haldane of England proposed that the first life came from pre-existing non-living organic molecules such as RNA and protein, and that this chemical evolution happened in the reducing conditions of early Earth with high temperature, volcanic storms and a reducing atmosphere of CH₄, NH₃ and others. In 1953 S.L. Miller created electric discharge in a closed flask containing CH₄, H₂, NH₃ and water vapour at 800 °C, and observed the formation of amino acids. The first non-cellular forms of life could have originated about 3 billion years back.
body.kn: ಒಪಾರಿನ್ ಮತ್ತು ಹಾಲ್ಡೇನ್ ರಾಸಾಯನಿಕ ವಿಕಾಸವನ್ನು ಪ್ರಸ್ತಾಪಿಸಿದರು. 1953ರಲ್ಲಿ ಮಿಲ್ಲರ್ CH₄, H₂, NH₃ ಮತ್ತು ನೀರಾವಿಯಲ್ಲಿ ವಿದ್ಯುತ್ ಕಿಡಿ ಹಾಯಿಸಿ ಅಮೈನೋ ಆಮ್ಲಗಳನ್ನು ಪಡೆದರು.

problem.en: In Miller's experiment, identify (a) what represented the early atmosphere, (b) what represented lightning, (c) the key product.

steps.en: (a) A closed flask with CH₄, H₂, NH₃ and water vapour at 800 °C modelled the reducing early atmosphere.
(b) Electric discharge from electrodes modelled lightning.
(c) Amino acids formed, showing organic molecules can arise from inorganic ones.

answer.en: (a) CH₄, H₂, NH₃, water vapour  (b) Electric spark  (c) Amino acids
